newsitem.title: USA: Teva's Copaxone cleared in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Teva's Copaxone cleared in Israel.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd said Thursday the Israeli Ministry of Health has cleared Copaxone to be marketed for the treatment of relapsing, remitting multiple sclerosis.
Israel is the first country to approve the drug. Teva expects to launch the product there before the end of the year.
The company said it was working to receive additional approvals in Britain, Canada, the United States and other countries, some of which require Israel's approval as a prerequisite.

On October 7, Teva received an "approvable letter" for Copaxone from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. That sets the stage to complete the remaining steps in gaining final approval to market the drug in the United States, the company noted.
